rationale.overall: B carries the reference's glassy, light-transmitting character — translucent overlaps, specular rim highlights and a glow under the triangle — where A renders the same geometry as opaque matte plastic on a flat fill.
rationale.material: B's rods let the triangle's edge and the ground show through where they cross and pick up sharp gloss along their lengths, plus a soft emissive bloom at the triangle's apex, all of which the REFERENCE has and A lacks entirely.
rationale.silhouette: The three-rod arrangement, angles, cap positions and squircle framing are effectively identical between A and B, so neither has an edge on outline read.
rationale.smallsize: At 32px and 16px both collapse to the same dark-cross-plus-orange-wedge motif with comparable contrast against the cream ground; B's marginally brighter wedge is not enough to separate them.

rationale.overall: The two takes are pixel-identical except for the bar rendering, and B's lighter, more translucent, more roundly-lit bars sit closer to the REFERENCE's glassy read, which is the deciding axis.
rationale.material: REF's bars are mid-grey translucent cylinders (mean bar luminance ~95) that transmit the orange beneath them; B's bars average ~65 with a broad soft specular band and visible warm transmission across the triangle, while A's average ~59 and read flatter and more opaque with only a thin hard highlight line.
rationale.silhouette: A difference image is black everywhere outside the bars — same bar geometry, same triangle, same squircle and background — so there is nothing to separate them on shape.
rationale.smallsize: At 32px and 16px A's darker bars hold marginally more separation from the cream field and leave the orange core slightly cleaner, where B's warmer bar-over-triangle transmission muddies the orange mass a little.
